whole_vs_partial_reasoning.conclusion: Each paragraph contains the complete substantive teaching of its own root. Whole-substantive classification is justified, with explicit omissions disclosed; this is not a word-for-word translation claim.
whole_vs_partial_reasoning.claims_retained: Every paragraph retains first-person single-thing/mind comparison, exact developed/undeveloped or guarded/tamed/etccondition, correct benefit/harm/pliant/happiness/suffering result, and repeated mind-specific conclusion.
whole_vs_partial_reasoning.vocatives: Source omits three occurrences of bhikkhave in every root. These repeated audience addresses are genuine omitted words and must be disclosed; no doctrinal assertion, condition or action is missing because of their omission.
whole_vs_partial_reasoning.paratext: Every root inline ordinal omitted; .21/.31chapterheadings and .30/.40chaptercolophons untranslated. Originalroottext and segment types remain intact.
whole_vs_partial_reasoning.negation_and_combo_controls: All positive/negative polarities verified, including unapparent/apparent .25/.26, uncultivated/cultivated .27–30 and allfour combined adjectives in .39/.40. No pair merged or counterpart skipped.
whole_vs_partial_reasoning.no_reconstructed_text: No rootbody has peyyala here; source contains no ellipsis. No generated/reconstructed English/Pali was used.
